title: Same patient but different worlds: A state-of-the-art review translating best practice psychosocial care from musculoskeletal care to the orthopaedic context
authors: Marie K. March; Katharine E. Roberts
pain_condition_detail: chronic musculoskeletal conditions including low back pain, knee osteoarthritis, shoulder pain, and whiplash disorder
bps_function_set: background framing; conclusion; intervention rationale; organizing principle; policy or practice implication
bps_operationalization_summary: The paper uses BPS as a rationale for integrating psychosocial care into orthopaedic surgery, organizing the review around psychosocial factors (psychological and social) with biological factors listed but not integrated. The BPS label frames the need for implementation but does not specify mechanisms linking domains.
integration_mechanism_summary: None proposed. The paper lists biological, psychological, and social factors as predictors of non-recovery but does not specify pathways or mechanisms linking them.
conceptual_tensions_1: Paper advocates BPS but focuses almost exclusively on psychosocial factors, biological domain is minimal
conceptual_tensions_2: Psychological resilience is named as important but authors note uncertainty about its definition and usefulness

additional_observations_2: Social domain is elaborated with specific factors (compensation, health literacy, cultural diversity) but not integrated with biological or psychological mechanisms
additional_observations_3: No psychological constructs are formally defined, all are named only
synthesis_note: This narrative review uses BPS language to justify integrating psychosocial care into orthopaedic surgery but operationalizes only psychological and social domains. Biological factors are listed but not developed. No cross-domain mechanisms are proposed. The paper is a practice-oriented implementation review, not a mechanistic account.

title: Same patient but different worlds: A state-of-the-art review translating best practice psychosocial care from musculoskeletal care to the orthopaedic context
authors: Marie K. March; Katharine E. Roberts
pain_condition_detail: Persistent/chronic musculoskeletal conditions in elective orthopaedic surgery, informed by musculoskeletal care.
context_note: Elective orthopaedic secondary care in hospital settings, with implementation lessons from primary-care musculoskeletal care and attention to women, culturally diverse and low-literacy communities.
bps_function_set: background framing; explanatory framework; intervention rationale; justification; organizing principle; policy or practice implication
bps_operationalization_summary: The paper operationalizes BPS mainly by translating psychosocial assessment, screening tools, interventions, workforce training, shared decision making, registries and equity implementation into orthopaedic care. It lists biological, psychological and social predictors but does not specify a three-domain mechanism.
integration_mechanism_summary: No detailed cross-domain mechanisms are proposed. The paper mainly states that biological, psychological and social factors predict poor recovery and that psychosocial assessment and intervention should be implemented in orthopaedics; the closest pathway is psychosocial assessment/intervention affecting outcomes.
conceptual_tensions_1: The paper says BPS requires interaction of physical, emotional and social factors, but the substantive review is mainly psychosocial implementation with biological factors mostly listed
conceptual_tensions_2: Screening tools for psychosocial risk are recommended in musculoskeletal care, yet orthopaedics lacks a universal comprehensive patient interview incorporating a biopsychosocial approach
conceptual_tensions_3: Decision aids are presented as shared decision-making tools, but the paper says decision aids without interactive processes have not improved surgical outcomes
conceptual_tensions_4: Multidisciplinary mental health care is recommended, but workforce costs and funding models are barriers
conceptual_tensions_5: Equity is emphasized for women and culturally diverse communities, but the paper says these groups have been excluded from research previously
additional_observations_1: The article is a state-of-the-art implementation review, not an effectiveness synthesis of BPS interventions
additional_observations_2: It uses primary-care musculoskeletal evidence to infer what orthopaedic surgery should implement
additional_observations_3: It treats psychosocial assessment as a screening and implementation task rather than as a validated three-domain model
additional_observations_4: Registry datasets are proposed as infrastructure for standardized psychosocial measurement
additional_observations_5: The paper foregrounds equity through women, ethnic minorities, language, literacy, and socio-gendered inequity
additional_observations_6: It mentions paediatric and adult cancer care only as analogies for implementation complexity
synthesis_note: This review uses the BPS label mainly to justify implementation of psychosocial assessment and care in orthopaedics. It lists biological, psychological and social predictors of poor recovery, but the analytic work is in psychosocial screening, interventions, workforce and implementation systems. It offers descriptive triadic linkage rather than a three-domain mechanism.
coding_rationale: BPS functions mainly as intervention rationale and organizing principle. Psychosocial and social content are elaborated, biology is mentioned, and triadic integration is descriptive only.

title: Same patient but different worlds: A state-of-the-art review translating best practice psychosocial care from musculoskeletal care to the orthopaedic context
authors: Marie K. March; Katharine E. Roberts
pain_condition_detail: chronic musculoskeletal conditions and elective orthopaedic surgery outcomes
context_note: Global perspective with specific attention to orthopaedic surgery contexts in primary and secondary care
bps_function_set: background framing; organizing principle; policy or practice implication
bps_operationalization_summary: Organizes the review around psychosocial care implementation in orthopaedic surgery, using BPS as a framing concept to structure discussion of barriers and solutions across multiple levels of healthcare delivery
conceptual_tensions_1: Tension between BPS theoretical integration and actual parallel listing of domains without specified mechanisms
conceptual_tensions_2: Uncertainty about psychological resilience definition and measurement utility in musculoskeletal contexts
conceptual_tensions_3: Gap between evidence of psychosocial factor associations and actual implementation of psychosocial care approaches in orthopaedic surgery
additional_observations_1: The review focuses primarily on psychological and social factors with minimal biological content, suggesting a psychosocial rather than fully biopsychosocial approach
additional_observations_2: Implementation barriers are discussed at multiple levels (individual, workforce, health service, societal) but without explicit integration mechanisms connecting these levels
additional_observations_3: The review emphasizes practical implementation challenges over theoretical integration of the BPS model
synthesis_note: This scoping review uses the biopsychosocial model as an organizing framework to explore psychosocial care implementation in orthopaedic surgery. It identifies psychological and social factors (depression, anxiety, catastrophizing, kinesiophobia, health literacy, compensation status, cultural diversity) but treats biological factors minimally. The review demonstrates multifactorial typology with no explicit integration mechanisms between domains, representing a gap between BPS theory and practical implementation in surgical contexts.
coding_rationale: Psychological and social domains scored elaborated due to multiple named constructs; biological scored mentioned due to limited constructs. Integration scored 'none' as domains listed in parallel without specified pathways. BPS typology 'multifactorial' as all three domains present but not integrated.
